findings.title: Recurring calendar deletions are not awaited after async getCalendar
findings.body: In the recurring cancellation branch, `bookingToDelete.user.credentials.filter(...).forEach(async (credential) => { const calendar = await getCalendar(credential); ... apiDeletes.push(deletedEvent); })` starts an async callback but the surrounding handler does not await it. `apiDeletes` may still be empty when `Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes))` runs, so external calendar events for recurring bookings may never be deleted. Rejections from `getCalendar` or `deleteEvent` are also unhandled. Replace this with a `for...of` loop plus `await`, or collect promises and await them explicitly.

findings.title: Reschedule does not await calendar/video deletion promises
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` awaits inside an async callback whose returned promise is ignored by `forEach`. The function continues to send the reschedule email without waiting for calendar or video deletions to complete, and errors from the dynamic import or deletion become unhandled promise rejections. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop with `await`.

findings.title: Reschedule does not await calendar/video deletion promises
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(...); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` awaits inside an async callback whose returned promise is ignored by `forEach`. The function continues to send the reschedule email without waiting for calendar or video deletions to complete, and errors from the dynamic import or deletion become unhandled promise rejections. Use `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop with `await`.

findings.title: requestReschedule does not await external calendar/video deletion
findings.body: `bookingRefsFiltered.forEach(async (bookingRef) => { ... const calendar = await getCalendar(credentialsMap.get(...)); return calendar?.deleteEvent(...); })` starts an async callback that `forEach` ignores. The mutation proceeds to send the reschedule email before the old calendar/video events are actually deleted, and any rejection from `getCalendar` or the deletion is unhandled. Replace with `Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(...))` or a `for...of` loop that awaits each operation.

findings.title: Dynamic import expressions are evaluated eagerly at module load
findings.body: The object literal calls `import("./applecalendar")`, `import("./caldavcalendar")`, etc. directly. These `import()` expressions start loading every listed app as soon as `@calcom/app-store` is imported, not when an entry is awaited. This does not give per-app lazy loading and can cause all app chunks to be fetched at startup. If lazy loading is intended, wrap each entry in a thunk such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` or use a lazy proxy.

findings.title: getCalendarCredentials now returns promise-valued calendar fields
findings.body: `getCalendar` is now async, but `getCalendarCredentials` remains synchronous and assigns `const calendar = getCalendar(credential);` without awaiting it. The exported function's effective return type changes from objects containing `Calendar` instances to objects containing `Promise<Calendar | null>`. The in-file consumer was updated to await `item.calendar`, but any other callers of this exported function that treat `calendar` as a `Calendar` will break. Consider making `getCalendarCredentials` async and awaiting each calendar, or explicitly documenting and updating all call sites.
